title: My content journey as an artist/student (0 → 15k)
subtitle: My lessons learned after a year of posting. AND my viral video frameworks for you to try!
excerpt: It took me years of thinking and wanting to make content before I actually did it. What made me post my first video? I made a bet with my best friend: if I don't post by the end of the week, I owe you $50.

title: Why you should post content!!
subtitle: The many worries of content creation and why you should post anyway, especially if you've been thinking about it!
excerpt: Content is incredibly fulfilling and learning the ropes is a journey unlike any other. It's an exponential game rather than a linear one, so you have to be patient, but once you get it, it will all be worth it.

title: as a creator, your friends might not support you
subtitle: and why it's okay
excerpt: After a year of posting, I've come to understand: your friends aren't your fans. It's unfair to expect them to be. And when I stopped expecting their commitment to me, I started creating freely.

title: your audience is your younger self
subtitle: the person you're meant to reach already knows you
excerpt: The most magnetic creators are speaking to one person, someone who they used to be before they figured something out. Your younger self was Googling questions late at night that you now know the answers to. That gap is your content.

title: minimum viable post (mvp)
subtitle: it doesn't have to be good. it just has to exist.
excerpt: It took me 2 years to post my first reel. I learned so much more in my first month of posting than I ever did in my 2 years of prepping and thinking. Done is infinitely better than indefinitely unfinished.

title: reaching flow state
subtitle: and my personal commandments for unlocking creativity to function in one's favor
excerpt: Work on what you love. Make time for the creative pursuit. Done over perfect. A mentor once advised me quantity over quality, and putting in the reps will yield much more progress than endlessly speculating on perfection.

title: an artist's brain never shuts off
subtitle: common pitfalls of the creative mind
excerpt: Overthinking. I do that a lot. For content, it means scrolling for inspiration when I'm actually just filling my mind with noise. For art, it means staring at a canvas and contemplating the next decision, instead of putting paint on the surface.

title: you need people who get it
subtitle: life is better when you surround yourself with them
excerpt: People who understand the path you're taking, who act as a sounding board at 3am for your ideas, will provide your fuel when you're exhausted and on the brink of giving up. Ambition and discipline can only get you so far.

title: how to never run out of ideas
subtitle: creativity is about nurturing your inner child with curiosity, delight, and wonder
excerpt: Creativity is like tuning a specific set of antennae to pick up on signals as you wander through your day-to-day. If you're feeling the creative block: what stories and lessons have you not yet told?

title: to be a creator in an AI world
subtitle: what does it mean when AI can generate anything with the snap of a finger?
excerpt: While AI is able to generate, automate, and assist, it cannot tell your story for you. Specificity, imperfection, vulnerability, and unlike-ness in a world of same-ness are the true boundaries separating human from AI-generated creation.

title: VYRA IS LIVE!!
subtitle: try the MCP connector today with an exclusive code :)
excerpt: Vyra just released our MCP connector, so you can now connect Vyra to your Claude, Cursor, or Codex/ChatGPT account and edit videos directly from there. My co-founder and I are so excited to have this out and in your hands.

title: creating vs. consuming
subtitle: what is your create-to-consume ratio?
excerpt: I can't create when I'm stuffed full with unnecessary, unmemorable information. Pen and paper first. Strike while it's hot. See the ideas through before the next one takes over.

title: the truth about growing on social media
subtitle: it's a long term game.
excerpt: It took me 30 flopped reels to hit my first viral video. I had no idea what I was doing but by throwing things at the wall for 3 months, something eventually clicked. Steal like an artist, and hooks are everything.
